# Envoy coordination: sessions, jobs, Convoy, and what rides back on every response

Companion to `/mcp-tools-reference`. The tool tables live there; this file holds the contracts behind the multi-session, job, bridge and Convoy tools and the fields that ride on every response. Without a skills folder, fetch it as `get_guidance(topic='mcp-tools-reference/coordination')`.

## Multi-session tools

- `get_sessions`: every AI client session connected to this Envoy (sid, label, pid, idle, last tool, `recent_scopes` = op paths and files recently modified, `claims` = scopes held, stale flag) plus `you` = the caller's own sid and `tasks` = the shared ledger's ACTIVE entries. Check it at session start and before large or destructive operations so concurrent sessions do not clobber each other. The response may include `worktrees`: in-flight durable worktree tasks, visible even after their session ended.
- `claim_scope(scope, note?, ttl?)`: a cooperative WRITE lease on an op-path prefix, a `file:<repo-relative>` path, or a `project:<name>` scope. Peers' overlapping claims are refused while yours is live; their destructive ops on it are gated. Auto-renews on your own writes; expires on TTL or session silence. `project:worktree-*` claims are DURABLE: they survive session death and Envoy restarts, expiring when the worktree directory is removed (7-day backstop). `release_scope(scope)` releases one early.
- `announce_task(title, scopes?, note?)`: a unit of work in the shared task ledger (`.embody/tasks.json`) so parallel sessions see what is being worked on and what is FINISHED but uncommitted. Announce at the start of substantive work; keep it honest with `update_task(task_id, status?, note?, commit?)`: `done_uncommitted` when finished but sitting in the tree (the state peers MUST see), `committed` with the sha once it lands (a sha alone implies the transition), `abandoned` when dropped. Any session may update any task; non-owner writes record `updated_by`.
- `preflight_landing(worktree_path)`: the landing safety check for a worktree diff. It intersects the files it would land with main-tree dirt, peer `file:` claims and touches, and unsaved live TDXN state in one call. Run it BEFORE porting any worktree diff; a `conflicts` verdict means reconcile first.

## Fields that ride on responses

- **`_logs`** rides along only when a WARNING or ERROR was logged during the call (capped at ~8); routine INFO/DEBUG/SUCCESS history is omitted. Warning cursors are per session, so concurrent sessions each receive their own copy. A `LAYOUT WARNING`, `THREADING WARNING`, `CONFLICT WARNING` or `MULTI-SESSION GATE` line is a hard stop: never end a turn without addressing it.
- **`_peers`** rides along when your request touches territory another session modified in the last ~10 minutes: one entry per peer, `{label, scope, tool, age_s, conflict}`. `conflict: true` means a peer WROTE an overlapping scope within the last minute AND your operation is also a write: stop, `get_sessions`, coordinate or divide the work by subtree, then proceed. Non-conflict advisories are informational and deduped per (peer, scope) for ~5 minutes; conflicts always ride. Load `/multi-session-etiquette` the moment one appears.
- **Destructive-op gate**: `delete_op`, `import_network` with `clear_first=True`, `run_tests`, and batches containing them are REFUSED (`MULTI-SESSION GATE` error naming the holder or peer) while a live peer session claims the scope or wrote it within the last minute. Pass `override=True` only when certain, and say so.
- **`recovery_hints`** ride on an `error`: each entry is `{code, cause, action, next_tools}` keyed off the message (path not found, wrong family, empty capture, thread conflict, timeout, ...). Recover by following it rather than retrying the same call verbatim. Every error envelope also carries `error_code` (`envoy.<area>.<condition>`, `envoy.error` when unclassified): branch on it, not on the message text.
- **`_effects`** ride on every write tool's response: errors and warnings that appeared after YOUR write, an fps drop, and for DAT writes the compile state of every GLSL operator consuming that DAT (`shaders_checked`, `new_shader_errors`, `shader_errors_persist`). Fix those before building further.
- **Unattended sessions**: nothing answers a dialog, so preset the Embody parameters that decide them: `Tdxnpalettehandling` (palette Black Box vs Full Export), `Filecleanup` (deleted-file prompt), `Tdxnlockedwarn` (`quiet`), `Tdxndatsafety` (save-time content report). Saves never prompt: save through `save_project` and read the save's warnings in `get_job_status(job_id)['warnings']`. When every tool times out, `list_dialogs` first.

## Jobs

Long operations that outlive the 30-second operation timeout run as disk-backed jobs (`.embody/jobs/`): the starting tool returns a `job_...` handle at once, results survive server restarts and extension reinits, and `get_job_status(job_id)` polls (omit the id to list the 16 newest records; finished records are kept 24 h).

- `run_tests(suite_name?, test_name?, override?, background?, idempotency_key?, confirm_saved?)`: Embody's unit-test suites (destructive and agent tiers excluded; they run only via their dedicated entry points). A FULL run is refused when the saved `.toe` is missing or over an hour old (it mutates the live network for ~25 minutes and that file is the only recovery point); `background=True` is the resilient mode for full runs, since the watchdog suites restart the server mid-run.
- `save_project(idempotency_key?)`: the save runs a few frames later so the response reaches the client before the main thread blocks on the TDXN strip/restore and the extension reinit. Refused while a test run is active. The finished record carries `version_before`, `version_after` and `warnings`.
- `update_embody(idempotency_key?)`: self-update to the latest GitHub release, bounded (sha256-pinned manifest, downgrade-refusing) and non-interactive; refused in Perform Mode and during test runs; the install restarts the server (one reconnect blip).
- `run_soak_test(...)`: the low-overhead performance soak; a running record carries `progress`, the finished one `result` with the verdict. Contract in `/testing`.
- `idempotency_key` on any of these makes a RETRY safe: a second call with the same key reconciles to the original job's handle instead of starting a duplicate.

## Bridge meta-tools

Served by the local STDIO bridge, so they work while TD is down or frozen.

- `get_td_status`: is TD running, is Envoy reachable, crash detection, process liveness, the instance registry, live bridge sessions; `envoy_unresponsive` and `main_thread_stalled` flag a TouchDesigner that is alive but frozen.
- `launch_td(timeout?)` and `restart_td(timeout?)`: launch or gracefully relaunch TD with the project's `.toe` and wait for Envoy (default 120 s).
- `list_dialogs(instance?, screenshot?)`: the modal dialogs a TD instance shows; runs on the bridge, so it answers while TD is blocked behind one. TD draws its own dialogs, so `screenshot=true` saves a PNG per dialog to Read. `blocked=true` when one is up.
- `dismiss_dialog(instance?, dialog?, action?)`: dismiss a blocking dialog and verify it is gone; `auto` runs close, escape, enter. Close and escape decline a question, enter accepts its default, so read the screenshot before choosing. Never targets the main window; `envoy.dialog.stuck` when nothing worked.
- `switch_instance(instance?, all_sessions?)`: list registered TD instances, or re-pin THIS session's bridge to another running instance. For a single call, pass `instance=<name>` on any Envoy tool instead; peers are untouched unless `all_sessions=true`. Workflow: `/multi-instance`.

## Convoy tools (LAN work relay)

Seventeen more meta-tools relay work to Convoy-enabled Embody nodes on the trusted LAN through the local per-user host app. Status and inventory calls (`get_convoy_status`, `convoy_list_nodes`, `convoy_list_controllers`, `convoy_ping`) never wake TouchDesigner.

- `convoy_select_node` pins THIS session to one exact node; ordinary Envoy tools then run there until `convoy_select_node` with `clear=true`.
- `convoy_call` / `convoy_batch` run registered operations on explicit one-off targets; pass a unique `idempotency_key` per intended action so a retry reconciles instead of double-running.
- `convoy_get_job` / `convoy_ack_job` / `convoy_cancel_job` reconcile durable deliveries; acknowledge a finished delivery you have safely observed so the target can release its protected result artifacts.
- `convoy_forget_node` deletes a stale node row on THIS machine's host app. It refuses only while the node has a delivery that has not FINISHED, and names the blocking delivery ids; dead and long-unseen rows are also evicted by the host's retention sweep.
- `convoy_get_artifact` / `convoy_save_artifact` fetch results BY ARTIFACT REFERENCE and verify them locally; never open a remote `C:\...` or `/Users/...` path as if it were local.
- `convoy_start_node` / `convoy_restart_node` manage node lifecycle; restarts require the node's CURRENT runtime id (from `convoy_list_nodes`) plus a unique `idempotency_key`, and the default policy refuses dirty or unverifiable project state.
- `convoy_update_embody` self-updates Embody on one node (`node=<id|name|hostname>`) or the whole fleet (`all=true`) as durable per-node jobs; offline, disabled and Perform Mode nodes are skipped by name.
- `convoy_owlette` is an optional read-mostly site bridge that fails closed without credentials.
- `convoy_lifecycle_state` / `convoy_lifecycle_quit` are reserved for the Convoy host's own lifecycle session; any other session gets `Convoy lifecycle host session required`. Use `convoy_restart_node` instead.
